title: SEATRACK data infrastructure
text: Overview database stucture diagram shows important tables database. logger new system, writes logger information logger_info Writes information start (mode, start time etc.) startup table. Writes information receive logger allocation table. Writes information logging session logging_session table. Writes basic information deployment deployment table. Writes information samples taken (blood, feathers etc.) sampling_events table. Also writes tables individuals schema, see . Writes basic information deployment observation table. Also writes tables individuals schema, see . Writes basic information deployment retrieval table. Writes information samples taken (blood, feathers etc.) sampling_events table. Also writes tables individuals schema, see . Writes information end session (date shutdown, logger status) shutdown table. logger registered succesful download status, writes expected files/filenames file_archive table. Writes information logging session logging_session table. Orange: individuals schema. Contains information individuals. - Current/permanent information sex age stored individ_info. individual one row table, row updated subsequent status. - Record status updates individ_status (breeding, size, etc.). written “encounter” individual (deployment, observation, retrieval) White: positions schema. Stores raw recorded/calculated position data. - Seperate tables different types positions: - postable: Positions derived GLS loggers. - gps_raw: GPS data. - gps_gsm_raw: GPS-GSM data. - irma_raw: GLS positions enhanced using IRMA. Currently empty. Dark blue: recordings schema. Stores types raw data recorded loggers. - Seperate tables different types recordings: - accelerometer_raw: Accelerometer data. - temperature_raw: Temperature data. - light_raw: Light data GLS loggers. - activity_raw: Immersion data. Green: metadata schema. Additional information linked tables. - Important tables include: - people: Table data responsible otherwise involved people. - species subspecies: Information species tracked. species also present subspecies table, species may one subspecies. - colony location: Information locations birds tracked. colony also present location table, colony may one location. - logger_models logger_producers: Information known logger models manufacturers. can see diagram, many tables directly connected logging_session. Many tables can therefore joined session_id. logger_id individ_id also useful columns present many tables. Individual status events can linked session first joining status encounter event (deployment, retrieval, observation) via status_id column found tables joining using session_id encounter table.

title: SEATRACK data infrastructure
text: number convenient views combine information: - loggers.session_details: provides comprehensive overview logging session, including deployment retrieval events data types available. - positions.postable, positions.gps, positions.gps_gsm: include positions extra metadata individual/logging session. - recordings.accelerometer, recordings.temperature, recordings.light, recordings.activity: include recording data extra metadata individual/logging session. - views.individual_info: combines individual statuses individual information logging session information. - views.logger_info: Combines summary logger start, allocation, deployment, retrieval shutdown. - individuals.ring_changes: Summary table individuals multiple ring numbers. scope adding additional views neccesary.

title: Extending seatrackR queries
text: Several seatrackR functions argument asTibble. default TRUE, meaning data requested collected database downloaded R local object. set argument FALSE, function instead return lazy query. Inspecting class returned object, can see tbl_PqConnection tbl_lazy. means data actually local R environment. try something like: get error. need use functions provided dbplyr dplyr work lazy data. packages translate R code SQL queries behind scenes. example: Note still considered table still lazy. haven’t actually got data yet. single variable, can use pull function: returns vector (case vector length 1) whole table, can use collect. Ideally, keep query lazy long possible. saves us downloading uneccesary data.
code: lazy_result <- getSessionInfo(     colony = "Røst",     species = "Atlantic puffin",     logger_type = "GLS",     has_positions = TRUE,     as_tibble = FALSE ) class(lazy_result) ## [1] "tbl_PqConnection" "tbl_dbi"          "tbl_sql"          "tbl_lazy"         "tbl" puffin_2024 <- lazy_result[lazy_result$deployment_year == 2024, ] # Filter the results to just 2024 unique_session_ids <- unique(puffin_2024$session_id) # Get unique session IDs n_session <- length(unique_session_ids) # Count the number of session IDs puffin_2024 <- filter(lazy_result, deployment_year == 2024) # Filter the results to just 2024 unique_session_ids <- distinct(puffin_2024, session_id) n_session <- count(unique_session_ids) n_session_local <- pull(n_session, n) # the count variable in n_sessions is n. print(n_session_local) ##
